methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $5.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 20.4x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Rapidus is a late-stage semiconductor company founded by Atsuyoshi Koike and Tetsuro Higashi that has raised $5.0B+ to date. The chips & semiconductors sector contains a diverse peer set of 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems, though few are directly comparable on stage and valuation tier.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method uses the $5.0B raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage financing rounds, yielding $6.0B. The peer-median method could not be executed due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables in semiconductors—while 13 same-sector peers exist, none met minimum thresholds for same-stage or adjacent-stage filtering. Public-comp anchoring was similarly inapplicable because Rapidus does not disclose revenue, precluding use of the 20.4x median P/S multiple observed across public semiconductor peers.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5.1B to $6.9B, with a central estimate of $6.0B. This range reflects limited triangulation capacity: reliance on a single method introduces material uncertainty. Key unknowns include Rapidus's actual revenue trajectory, margin profile relative to public peers, and stage-specific funding velocity in semiconductor venture markets. Tighter valuation would require either disclosed financials or a larger cohort of directly comparable late-stage semiconductor investments.
